chunks: And a group informed us, from Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Quluwayh and Abu Ghalib al-Zarari and Abu Muhammad al-Talakbari, all of them, from Muhammad ibn Yaqub, from Ishaq ibn Yaqub, who said:

I asked Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari, may Allah have mercy on him, to deliver to me a letter in which questions had been asked about matters that had baffled me. The response came in the handwriting of our Master, the Patron of the House, peace be upon him: 'As for Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari, may Allah be pleased with him and his father before him, he is my trusted one and his letter is my letter.'

key_terms.ثِقَتِي: My trusted one / my reliable one
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الدَّارِ: The Patron of the House (a title for the Imam)
key_terms.مَسَائِلَ أَشْكَلَتْ عَلَيَّ: Matters that were unclear/baffling to me

ai.seo_question: Who is Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari and what is his status according to the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the principle of *tawqi'* (the Imam's handwritten signature) as a primary source of authority, confirming that Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari’s personal correspondence carried the same weight as the Imam’s own words. It underscores the legitimacy of the *Nuwwab al-Arba'a* (Four Deputies) during the Minor Occultation, illustrating how the Imam maintained direct, authenticated communication with his representatives to guide the community in the absence of his physical presence.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 326 - A group narrated to us from Abul Qasim Ja’far Ibn Muhammad Ibn Quluwayh and Abu Ghalib Razi and Abu Muhammad Talakbari, all of whom narrate from Muhammad Ibn Yaqub on the authority of Ishaq Ibn Yaqub, who says:

I asked Muhammad Ibn Uthman Amari to deliver a letter of mine, in which I had asked about some queries that had baffled me. The answer in the handwriting of our Master the Patron of the House came stating, “As for Muhammad Ibn Uthman Amari, may Allah be pleased with him and his father before him: he has my full trust and his letter is my letter.”
